on nonzero exits; do not treat scope/no-evidence responses as subprocess crashes.
Unknown editions and incompatible resource hashes fail closed. Topic relevance is
lexical, not proof of applicability. Combined evidence keeps whole prerequisite
bundles within 100 nodes / 24,000 serialized characters; omissions are explicit.

## Example integration without coupling

A consumer sends a domain question, its purpose and known context. It parses the
bundle, checks `contract_version`, uses explanations for orientation, and checks
`evidence_status`, `review_state`, each `applies_to` and `required_actions` before
using claims. It retains release/claim/source identifiers in its own work product.
It owns all writing, review, approvals and external actions. A failed domain lookup
must not silently become an invented requirement or guessed parameter.

`srs-network`: request semantics, exceptions and source strength for its proposed
requirement. Design skill: request tradeoffs, constraints and required project
inputs. Test skill: request observable behavior, allowed alternatives and source
issues, then define and execute its own configured test. Direct user: explain the
concept with an example, then offer the relevant deeper evidence and limitations.

## Optional Python adapter

`src/retrieval/client.py` exposes `request_knowledge(skill_root, query, purpose=...,
versions=..., platform=..., role=..., timeout=30, consumer='general')` using only the standard library.
It can be loaded by absolute path without changing the consumer working directory:

```python
import importlib.util
from pathlib import Path
root = Path("/installed/network-domain-knowledge")
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("network_knowledge_client", root / "src/retrieval/client.py")
client = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(client)
bundle = client.request_knowledge(root, "Can retry repeat an operation?", purpose="explain")
# Pass the entire bundle to the consumer's reasoning/review step.
# Do not discard evidence_status, issues, conditions or required_actions.
```

The adapter preserves NEEDS_SCOPE/CONFLICT/NO_EVIDENCE as normal structured results,
rejects incompatible contract versions and inconsistent exit/status pairs, and
raises on execution/provider errors or timeout. It uses an argument list without
a shell, never uploads records, and never grants approval. Production use still
needs verification in the actual consuming skill and environment.

## Compatibility and update

Existing search/show/source/tests contracts are retained. Stable topic/claim IDs
must not be reused for different meanings. Optional additions to v1 are allowed;
removal, renamed fields or changed status meaning require a new contract version.
Treat unknown fields as extensions but reject unsupported major contract versions.
Record release changes and re-run consumer contract tests after upgrades. Stop
consumers during installation replacement; run doctor --full before switching and
restore the prior complete validated tree for rollback. Checksums detect accidental
change; they are not signed publisher authentication.

## Consultation retrieval roles and OS evidence boundary

Consultation ranks general protocol knowledge before TC8 test evidence for
ordinary questions. Explicit test IDs, `--purpose test`, and test wording retain
access to test evidence; exact claim IDs retain their original retrieval path.
The low-level `search` command remains a lexical evidence lookup. Scope, prerequisite and conflict expansion still run
after candidate ranking; related evidence is not another direct answer.

Optional v1 fields:

- `evidence_roles`: classification by claim reference: protocol knowledge, test
  evidence, power/link protocol, AUTOSAR platform reference, source issue or
  unclassified. Concept explanations and design recommendations retain their
  existing classifications. Roles describe navigation, not normative authority.
- `reference_evidence`: scoped common background that cannot establish the requested
  OS implementation behavior. Preserve its source qualifications and linked issues,
  but never cite it as evidence of Linux, Android or QNX behavior.

The corpus includes bounded reviewed Linux/Android/QNX documentation references;
this does not establish broad OS or product coverage. OS-specific requests can
still return `NO_EVIDENCE` or `NEEDS_SCOPE`, with common background separated from
applicable evidence. Explanations and navigation routes may remain available.
For QNX networking, use the [focused Wiki index](qnx8-network-review.md) and its
source snapshots for bounded lookup when ordinary discovery is insufficient.
Check the actual returned statuses, source conditions and missing product inputs;
do not infer unsupported protocols or verified deployment from these boundaries.

Ranking uses lexical term coverage, source roles and bounded topic heuristics;
it is not semantic entailment. Querying AP alone does not search for Adaptive
abbreviations. Explicit AUTOSAR/Adaptive questions can still retrieve those claims.
The ranking checks cover selected regressions, not universal search precision.

## Content-reviewed classifications

`content_roles` is an optional v1 map for returned evidence/background. Each entry
has a primary role, secondary roles, a rationale and a basis: `content_review` or
`source_derived`. Mixed test/integration material retains test evidence as primary
unless the reviewed text is explanatory guidance rather than a test procedure.
`integration_guidance` is explanatory, not a new normative rule. All current
claims have explicit content-role reviews of the Wiki text. This is navigation
classification, not renewed source verification or independent technical approval.
New production claims require a role review; synthetic fixtures may retain fallback
source-derived classification. Original scope and source issue qualifications remain mandatory.

The unsupported-domain boundary also covers explicit VLAN/PCP/TSN/gPTP, DoIP/UDS,
and authentication/authorization/TLS/MACsec/IPsec questions. These requested domains
lack reviewed implementation/standard coverage. Common background can still help,
but does not establish their rules. At most five gap entries are returned; the
limitation detail lists all detected missing domain IDs. Keyword detection is
conservative and cannot recognize every paraphrase or infer all intended scope.

### Acquired sources awaiting review

A source gap with `acquired_pending_review` carries a SHA-256 identifying an
acquired document, not approved evidence or complete coverage of the gap.
`reviewed_sections` remains empty. Candidate and blocked entries retain null hashes.
For multi-document gaps the reason identifies the hashed document and remaining
work. Documentation indexes are navigation only. Consumers must not promote any
intake state into claims or remove OS/domain abstention based on acquisition.

### Domain-specific scope

Use [SOME/IP evidence](someip-guide.md) for CP Transformer/TP and SD editions,
[Ethernet evidence](ethernet-guide.md) for bounded Linux references, and
[support and limitations](support-and-limitations.md) for current coverage.
Optional implementation sources require explicit selection or matching discovery;
protocol evidence alone cannot establish product implementation behavior.

### Reference discovery routes (optional v1 extension)

`reference_routes` returns up to five non-normative source pointers matched to the
question. Each includes source_id, version, claim_refs and a scope disclaimer.
It does not modify request.source_versions, turn NO_EVIDENCE into OK, or certify
project applicability. Consumers may present these pointers and request the
relevant source edition for bounded lookup. Routes are not quote/evidence objects.

Use [coverage-inventory.json](coverage-inventory.json) to distinguish zero-claim acquired sources from bounded
reviewed claims; no document is marked completely reviewed. Use recovery-review-workflow.md for project-owned design oracles and handoff fields.

### Bounded QNX manual lookup (optional v1 extension)

For a QNX-only request naming an API or utility in the focused network index,
`documentation_lookup` separates manual-description evidence from the existing
broad product/OS evidence boundary. Topic discovery uses explicit identifiers in
the hash-checked scope manifest, not general keyword overlap. Matching routes
include the exact source snapshot and claim references. Unscoped lookup returns
`NEEDS_SCOPE`; no source version is selected automatically. With the explicit
edition, the lookup returns the selected topic's claims and mandatory dependencies.
A mismatching edition cannot substitute another snapshot. `issues`, role maps and
consumer retention instructions also cover this bundle.

Its own `status`, `evidence`, `limitations` and `scope` must be retained. An `OK`
manual lookup supports a qualified explanation of documented behavior; it does
not change broad `evidence_status`, establish installed BSP/driver applicability,
or prove timing, safety or protocol conformance. Unsupported broader questions
still require additional evidence. Mixed-OS questions do not automatically select
the QNX manual lane. Generic or unnamed topics continue to use ordinary routes
and the focused index. This is bounded lexical discovery, not semantic question
understanding. The lookup has a separate 100-node/24,000-character evidence budget;
whole prerequisite bundles are omitted with an explicit limitation if needed.

### General QNX diagnostic questions (optional v1 extension)

`question_guidance` contains one curated diagnostic profile when a QNX-only
question matches all signal groups for a supported symptom. It supplies an
English diagnostic sequence, required observations and linked knowledge IDs;
the host explains these in the user's language. It is non-normative guidance,
not a discovered root cause. Matching uses bilingual patterns from an
integrity-checked resource; no OS or source edition is guessed from a bare symptom.

The profile supplies relevant `reference_routes` when no explicit API/utility
topic was found. These topics use the same scoped `documentation_lookup` path.
If topics span different archive batches under `QNX-SDP-DOCSET`, retrieve each
edition in a separate request; the existing source-version map selects one
edition per source. Retain each returned bundle and its issue context. A partial
single-edition response is not the complete cross-topic explanation.

The build validates the profile schema, regular expressions and knowledge IDs.
Unknown, ambiguous or unsupported questions remain outside this bounded route
set. Explicit API topics keep precedence. Consumers must retain `question_guidance`
when present, along with the documentation and applicability fields.

## Reusable expert handoff extension

The optional `--consumer general|srs|test_case|diagnosis` selects a handoff without
changing purpose, source versions or existing v1 status meanings. The Python
adapter accepts `consumer` too. The response adds `expert_knowledge`,
`consumer_guidance` and `retrieval_breakdown`; all are retained across agent calls.
See [the expert guide](expert-knowledge-guide.md) for schemas, lifecycle and examples.
The question lookup status is separated from supplemental lookups for diagnosis;
it is not a replacement for aggregate evidence_status or applicability review.
An expert record's supporting_claim_refs are navigation until scoped retrieval has
returned their full source and prerequisite bundles. Draft/retired/internal-only
records are excluded from deployment. Schema validity is not human approval.

SOMEIP-K-0001#C2 The SOME/IP header Length field counts the bytes from the beginning of the Request ID to the end of the message. The total message length is Length + 8. For a basic message without additional headers, Length is 8 plus the payload byte count, and the total size is 16 plus the payload byte count.

SOMEIP-K-0034#C1 All non-final TP segment-data lengths shall be multiples of 16 bytes. This counts segment payload bytes, excluding the SOME/IP and TP headers. A correctly aligned maximum segment-data length of 1392 bytes is recommended, not an unconditional maximum for every deployment.

SOMEIP-K-0034#C2 Senders shall segment only messages configured for segmentation and send segments in ascending order. Non-final segments shall have equal sizes, and the sender shall try to maximize segment size within specification limits.

SOMEIP-K-0033#C2 Each TP segment sets the Message Type TP flag and inserts a four-byte big-endian TP header immediately after the SOME/IP header. From high to low bits it contains a 28-bit Offset, three reserved bits and one More Segments bit.

SOMEIP-K-0029#C1 UDP binding carries SOME/IP messages in UDP packets and shall not prohibit UDP fragmentation. The recommended payload range is 0..1400 bytes; larger payloads should use TCP or segmentation rather than treating 1400 as an unconditional validity limit.

SOMEIP-K-0039#C4 Return Codes 0x10..0x1F are reserved for generic SOME/IP errors, while 0x20..0x5E are reserved for service/method-specific errors defined by the interface. An error message with a generic error Return Code in 0x01..0x1F shall not trigger another error message.

SOMEIP-K-0014#C1 The base Message Type values are REQUEST=0x00, REQUEST_NO_RETURN=0x01, NOTIFICATION=0x02, RESPONSE=0x80 and ERROR=0x81. REQUEST expects a response even for a void method; notifications and fire-and-forget requests do not.

SOMEIP-K-0014#C3 Every header carries Return Code. REQUEST, REQUEST_NO_RETURN and NOTIFICATION shall set it to E_OK (0x00); ERROR shall not use E_OK. RESPONSE may convey a configured nonzero application return code.

SOMEIP-K-0051#C2 An RPC invokes a method on another ECU. Request/Response exchanges invocation and result messages; fire-and-forget omits the response. Events are one-way updates sent cyclically or on change, while a field represents a current status accessed by getter, setter and notifier.

SOMEIP-K-0040#C2 For a Request/Response error message, copy Message ID, Request ID and Interface Version from the request, but not its payload. Set the appropriate Message Type and Return Code; explicit ERROR payloads carry interface-defined serialized error information.

SOMEIP-K-0042#C1 The general Message Type rule says errors on a regular request produce ERROR, whereas detailed application-error rules retain RESPONSE when no extended information is needed and use ERROR when it is. Review these provisions together; do not classify every nonzero application Return Code as Message Type ERROR.

NEEDS_SCOPE NEEDS_SCOPE
SOMEIP-SD-2208#C1 R22-11 PRS_SOMEIPSD_00434 전이 본문(p.57)은 interface가 up_and_configured이거나 service가 up인 초기 조건도 Not Ready로 가는 것으로 적지만, Figure 5.16(p.60)은 두 조건을 AND로 묶어 Ready로 진입한다. 또한 00411(p.54)은 Main 진입 후 첫 Offer까지 CYCLIC_OFFER_DELAY 한 주기를 기다리도록 하지만 상태 전이 본문(p.59)과 그림의 Main 진입 action에는 timer 설정과 send(OfferService)가 함께 있다. 이 차이를 임의로 통합해 실행 상태 머신이나 정밀 타이밍 시험 oracle을 생성하지 않는다. 적용 판본의 정오표·공급자 해석·프로젝트 결정을 확인해야 하며, 이 기록은 어느 표현이 우선한다는 결론이 아니다.

SOMEIP-SD-2204#C3 R22-11 PRS_SOMEIPSD_00427은 Repetition/Main의 서버 서비스가 중단될 때 StopOffer를 보내도록 한다. 00428–00429는 서버가 StopOffer를 송신하면 서버 측, 클라이언트가 수신하면 클라이언트 측의 해당 서비스 인스턴스 구독을 모두 삭제하도록 한다. 00430은 StopOffer를 받은 클라이언트가 FindService를 보내지 않고 Offer 또는 애플리케이션·네트워크 관리·Ethernet 링크 등의 상태 변화를 기다리도록 한다. 00431은 Main의 클라이언트 서비스가 해제될 때 가입한 모든 Eventgroup에 StopSubscribe를 보내도록 한다. 00751에서 서버 링크가 Initial Wait/Repetition/Main 중 내려가면 Down으로 가고 링크가 복구되…

SOMEIP-SD-2202#C2 R22-11 PRS_SOMEIPSD_00350은 서비스 상태를 모르는 경우, 즉 현재 유효한 Offer가 없는 경우에만 FindService를 보내도록 한다. 00351은 FindService TTL을 사용하지 않으며 임의 값으로 설정할 수 있고 수신자는 이를 무시하도록 한다. 따라서 FindService의 TTL=0을 StopOffer나 구독 해제로 해석하지 않는다. 00528–00530에서 FindService 송신자는 Endpoint/Multicast Option을 참조하지 않고 수신자는 그러한 옵션을 무시하지만, 다른 종류의 옵션까지 일괄 금지하지는 않는다.

SOMEIP-SD-2202#C3 R22-11 Service Entry TTL은 24비트 초 단위 값이다. PRS_SOMEIPSD_00356에서 OfferService(type 0x01)의 TTL은 서비스 제공 유효기간이며 만료 후에는 제공 중으로 보지 않는다. 0xFFFFFF는 다음 재부팅까지 유효하고, 0은 Offer가 아니라 StopOffer이다. 00364와 00840은 StopOffer가 중단하려는 Offer와 같은 엔트리 필드 및 옵션을 사용하되 TTL을 0으로 설정하도록 한다. 이 TTL을 애플리케이션 응답시간 보장이나 장애 복구 완료 시간으로 사용하지 않는다.

SOMEIP-SD-2208#C2 R22-11 PRS_SOMEIPSD_00435 전이 본문(p.63)은 Service Ready에서 Stopped로 가는 트리거를 receive(OfferService)로 적지만 Figure 5.17(p.65)은 receive(StopOfferService)와 cancelTimer(TTL)을 표시한다. 같은 본문은 Requested_but_not_ready에서 Searching으로 가는 interface 조건을 !=up_and_configured로 쓰지만 그림은 ==up_and_configured를 표시한다. 초기 Requested_but_not_ready 진입도 본문(p.61)의 Service Not Requested와 그림의 ServiceRequested 표현이 다르다. 그림을 시각적으로 확인했으나 이 차이를 공식 정정으로 처리하지 않는다. 텍스트만으로 자동 상태 코드를 생성하거나 전이 시험 합격 기준을 확정하지 말고 이슈를 유지…

SOMEIP-SD-2201#C1 R22-11 §1.3.1과 PRS_SOMEIPSD_00220은 SOME/IP-SD를 UDP로 전송하도록 규정한다. SOME/IP 자체가 TCP와 UDP를 지원한다는 사실을 SD의 TCP 전송 허용으로 해석하지 않는다. §5.1.2.1의 SD 메시지는 Service ID 0xFFFF, Method ID 0x8100, Client ID 0x0000, Protocol Version 0x01, Interface Version 0x01, Message Type 0x02(Notification), Return Code 0x00(E_OK)를 사용한다. 이는 SD 메시지 형식에 관한 규칙이며 개별 서비스의 버전·포트·전송 프로토콜과 구분한다.

SOMEIP-SD-2201#C3 R22-11 PRS_SOMEIPSD_00157–00160에 따라 SD 송신 Session ID는 메시지마다 증가하며 1에서 시작하고 wrap 이후에도 1이며 0을 사용하지 않는다. §5.1.2.2의 00255·00256·00631은 Reboot Flag를 재부팅 후 Session ID가 처음 wrap할 때까지 1, 그 후 0으로 유지하며 송신·수신, multicast·unicast 및 sender-receiver 관계를 구분해 상태를 관리하도록 한다. 본문 주석상 송신은 multicast 카운터 하나와 unicast 상대별 카운터, 수신은 multicast와 unicast 각각 상대별 카운터를 둔다. ECU 전체에 단일 수신 Session ID를 공유하는 것으로 해석하지 않는다.

SOMEIP-SD-2201#C2 R22-11 PRS_SOMEIPSD_00153의 SOME/IP Length는 길이 필드 바로 다음 바이트부터 SD 메시지 마지막 바이트까지의 바이트 수이다. PRS_SOMEIPSD_00265의 Entries Array 및 Options Array 앞 uint32 길이는 각각 뒤따르는 배열 데이터의 바이트 수이며 엔트리 개수나 옵션 개수가 아니다. PRS_SOMEIPSD_00263은 엔트리를 도착한 순서 그대로 처리하도록 한다. 이 항목은 길이 의미와 순서를 설명하며 전체 malformed-message 처리 정책을 정의하지 않는다.

SOMEIP-SD-2201#C4 R22-11 PRS_SOMEIPSD_00258은 해당 통신 상대의 직전 수신값(old)과 현재 값(new)을 비교해 (old.reboot=0 AND new.reboot=1) OR (old.reboot=1 AND new.reboot=1 AND old.session_id>=new.session_id)이면 재부팅으로 판정한다. new.reboot=1만 보거나 old.reboot 조건을 생략한 Session ID 비교는 이 규칙을 대체하지 못한다. 비교 상태의 통신 관계별 분리는 C3을 함께 적용한다. 이 항목은 직전 값과 현재 값의 판정에 한정되며 최초 수신 초기화, 서비스·구독 무효화 및 복구 완료 조건은 별도 검토 대상이다.

SOMEIP-SD-2202#C1 R22-11 PRS_SOMEIPSD_00833 및 00341–00343에서 option run은 Options Array의 첫 옵션 인덱스와 옵션 개수로 표현한다. 인덱스 0은 첫 옵션이며 바이트 오프셋이 아니다. 개수 0인 run은 비어 있고 송신 시 해당 인덱스도 0으로 설정한다. 그러나 00834는 수신한 run의 개수가 0이면 인덱스가 0이 아니어도 메시지를 수락하고 처리하도록 명시한다. 송신 형식 제약을 그대로 수신 거부 조건으로 적용하지 않는다. 이 예외가 범위 밖 옵션 참조 등 다른 오류까지 허용한다는 뜻은 아니다.

SOMEIP-SD-2203#C1 R22-11 PRS_SOMEIPSD_00386의 SubscribeEventgroup은 type 0x06이고 TTL은 구독 유효기간이며 0xFFFFFF는 다음 재부팅까지 유효하다. 00389·00574에서 StopSubscribeEventgroup은 중단할 Subscribe와 같은 필드·옵션을 사용하되 TTL=0이다. 00390–00391에서 Ack는 수락을 뜻하며 type 0x07이고 Service ID, Instance ID, Major Version, Eventgroup ID, TTL, Reserved, Counter를 응답 대상 Subscribe에서 유지한다. 00393–00394에서 Nack도 type 0x07이지만 거부를 뜻하고 TTL=0이며 나머지 지정 필드는 응답 대상과 같다. 00829는 Ack/Nack의 Service ID·Instance ID·Eventgroup ID·Major Version을 해당 Subscribe와 정확히 맞춰 식별하도록 한다. type만으로 A

SOMEIP-SD-2203#C2 R22-11 PRS_SOMEIPSD_00386(PDF p.48)은 SubscribeEventgroup TTL=0 설명에서 Stop Offer Service Entry라는 이름을 사용한다. 반면 00389(p.50)는 Subscribe와 같은 필드에 TTL=0인 것을 StopSubscribeEventgroup으로 정의하며, 00270(p.27)은 Subscribe와 StopSubscribe의 type을 0x06으로 명시한다. 이 명칭 불일치를 숨기거나 Subscribe를 StopOffer(type 0x01)로 자동 변환하지 않는다. 관련 조항을 함께 검토하고 프로젝트 해석을 명시해야 한다. 공식 정오표나 R23-11에서의 해결 여부는 아직 확인하지 않았다.
